question.text: 'Ganga Strategic Fund' (Cat II AIF) is negotiating a side-letter granting one strategic anchor LP an 'excess loss absorption' right not granted to other LPs. Under SEBI's pro-rata / pari-passu framework (Fifth Amendment, November 2024), what is the compliance position?

answer.text: Permissible — side letters are always permitted if signed before First Close

Pro-rata rights to investors apply by default; differential rights may be offered subject to SFA implementation standards, with PPM disclosures; 'priority distribution model' (where one class absorbs disproportionate losses) is PROHIBITED for fresh commitments / new investee investments post Nov 18, 2024; only specified entities (Manager/Sponsor, DFIs, SIDCs, Government-controlled entities, Central Banks, SWFs) may subscribe to junior/subordinate classes
All side-letters are banned for AIFs without exception
Side-letters are permitted only in LVFs

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) (Fifth Amendment) Regulations, 2024 and Circular dated Dec 16, 2024: pro-rata rights are the default; priority distribution model (differential loss-sharing) prohibited for fresh commitments; pari-passu exception for Manager/Sponsor, multilateral/bilateral DFIs, SIDCs, Government/Central-Bank/SWF entities (these may subscribe to junior classes). Differential rights must not: (a) create inter-investor liability, (b) give control outside IC, (c) alter other investors' existing rights. All differential rights must be transparently disclosed in the PPM. Pari-passu rule does not apply to AI-only Funds. The Trap: Option A ignores the 2024 amendment. Option C overstates the ban. Option D creates a false LVF-exclusive rule. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C is the primary exam that tests the Fifth Amendment. Compliance exams (III-A/C) also cover it. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: Report non-SFA-standard differential rights to SEBI via aifreporting@sebi.gov.in in the prescribed format. Immediately terminate rights that adversely affect other investors. Evergreening of liabilities (Manager/Sponsor junior units being indirectly repaid by investee companies) is prohibited and flagged in Compliance Test Report.
